questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
He is senior / than me / in the organisation.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'than me'. 'Senior' takes 'to': 'senior to me'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Scarcely any / of the funds / were spent on administration.
questions.x: The sentence is grammatically correct as written. Correct: 'any of the funds' with plural 'were'.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To be in the doldrums'
o: To be in a state of inactivity or low spirits
questions.x: 'To be in the doldrums' means: to be in a state of inactivity or low spirits.

questions.q: Scarcely had the inspection ended ____ the workers resumed production.
questions.x: 'Scarcely…when' is the correct pair.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Indolent'.
questions.x: 'Indolent' is the opposite of 'Industrious'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Indolent'.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: CANDOUR
questions.x: 'Candour' means openness. 'Deceit' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Placate'.
questions.x: 'Placate' means pacify. 'Provoke' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: LETHARGIC
questions.x: 'Lethargic' means sluggish. 'Energetic' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To keep one's head above water'
o: To manage to survive, especially financially
questions.x: 'To keep one's head above water' means: to manage to survive, especially financially.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Belligerent'.
questions.x: 'Belligerent' is the opposite of 'Peaceable'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Belligerent'.

questions.q: What is the author's attitude towards informal settlements?
o: They are eyesores that must be removed
They are irrelevant to urban growth
They should be shifted outside cities
They are economically valuable and should be upgraded rather than cleared
questions.x: Answer: 'They are economically valuable and should be upgraded rather than cleared'. The author calls them 'engines of the urban economy' and recommends upgrading services in place. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Cities in India are growing faster than their planners can imagine. Migrants arrive with skills and ambition, but often find shelter only in informal settlements without clean water or sanitation. Yet these neighbourhoods are not merely problems to be cleared; they are engines of the urban economy, supplying labour to construction, transport and domestic work. Planners who treat them only as eyesores risk destroying the livelihoods that keep the city running. A wiser approach is to upgrade services where people already live.

questions.q: The word 'eyesores' in the passage most nearly means:
questions.x: Answer: 'Ugly or unpleasant sights'. An eyesore is something unpleasant to look at. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Cities in India are growing faster than their planners can imagine. Migrants arrive with skills and ambition, but often find shelter only in informal settlements without clean water or sanitation. Yet these neighbourhoods are not merely problems to be cleared; they are engines of the urban economy, supplying labour to construction, transport and domestic work. Planners who treat them only as eyesores risk destroying the livelihoods that keep the city running. A wiser approach is to upgrade services where people already live.

questions.q: The 'Kol uprising' (1831–32) occurred in:
questions.x: Correct answer: Chotanagpur. The Kols protested against transfer of land to outsiders.

questions.q:
Consider the following leaders:
1. Gopal Krishna Gokhale
2. Pherozeshah Mehta
3. Bipin Chandra Pal
4. Surendranath Banerjee
How many of the above were Moderates?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Gokhale, Mehta and Banerjee were Moderates; Pal was an Extremist.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the first official census (1872, non-synchronous) and creation of an agriculture department?
questions.x: Lord Mayo was Viceroy during the first official census (1872, non-synchronous) and creation of an agriculture department.

questions.q: The 'Swadeshi' movement of 1905 included all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Non-payment of land revenue across India
questions.x: Correct answer: Non-payment of land revenue across India. Non-payment of revenue was not part of the 1905 programme.

questions.q:
In which year did the following take place?
The Hindustan Republican Association was formed at Kanpur.
questions.x: The Hindustan Republican Association was formed at Kanpur in 1924. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: The 'Hunter Commission' of 1882 concerned:
questions.x: The 1919 Hunter Committee was a different body that inquired into the Punjab disturbances.

questions.q: Who founded the Prarthana Samaj (1867)?
questions.x: The Prarthana Samaj (1867) was founded by Atmaram Pandurang.

questions.q: The newspaper/journal 'Comrade' is associated with:
o: Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendranath Dutta
questions.x: 'Comrade' was started/edited by Maulana Mohammad Ali.

questions.q: Who presided over the 1928 session of the Indian National Congress held at Calcutta?
questions.x: Motilal Nehru presided over the 1928 Calcutta session — the session that considered the Nehru Report.

questions.q: The Khilafat movement was led by:
o: Ali brothers (Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali)
questions.x: Gandhi joined it to forge Hindu–Muslim unity in the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.q: Who became President of the United States in January 2025?
questions.x: Correct answer: Donald Trump. He began his second, non-consecutive term on 20 January 2025.

questions.q: Which day is observed on 23 April?
questions.x: 23 April is World Book and Copyright Day.

questions.q: The SCO Heads of State Council summit in 2025 was held in:
questions.x: Correct answer: Tianjin, China. India hosted the SCO virtually in 2023.

questions.q: Single-use plastic items with low utility were banned in India from:
questions.x: The ban was notified under the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2021.

questions.q: The military exercise 'Dustlik' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'Dustlik' is a bilateral exercise between India and Uzbekistan.

questions.q: Under the Deep Ocean Mission, India's crewed submersible being developed for depths of 6,000 m is called:
questions.x: Correct answer: Matsya-6000 (Samudrayaan). It will carry three people to explore deep-sea resources.

questions.q: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded for the development of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Metal–organic frameworks. Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi were honoured.

questions.q: Which State became the first to implement a Uniform Civil Code, in January 2025?
questions.x: Goa has had a civil code since Portuguese times, but Uttarakhand is the first State to enact and implement a UCC law after independence.

questions.q: Which of the following organisations is headquartered in London?
questions.x: International Maritime Organization is based in London.

questions.q: At the Paris Paralympics 2024, India's total medal tally was:
questions.x: Correct answer: 29. It included seven gold medals — India's best Paralympics performance.

questions.q: The constitutional amendment that affirmed Parliament's power to amend any part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights was enacted in the year:
questions.x: This was the 24th Amendment Act, 1971.

questions.q: NITI Aayog, which replaced the Planning Commission, was set up on:
questions.x: It is a non-constitutional, non-statutory body; the PM is its chairperson.

questions.q: If the offices of both the President and Vice-President fall vacant, who acts as President?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.x: This happened in 1969 when Chief Justice M. Hidayatullah acted as President.

questions.q: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee, relates to:
o: Simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies ('One Nation, One Election')
questions.x: It proposes Article 82A and changes to terms of legislatures; it followed the Ram Nath Kovind committee's report.

questions.q: A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed by:
o: An order of the President after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a special majority on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity
A simple majority in the Lok Sabha
questions.x: Correct answer: An order of the President after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a special majority on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. Article 124(4) and the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.

questions.q: Article 81 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Superintendence, direction and control of elections vested in an Election Commission
Composition of the House of the People (Lok Sabha)
questions.x: Article 81: Composition of the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

questions.q: The Citizenship (Amendment) Rules were notified, operationalising the CAA, in:
questions.x: The rules enabled applications for citizenship by eligible migrants who entered India on or before 31 December 2014.

questions.q: Which Parliamentary committee is the largest and has members only from the Lok Sabha?
questions.x: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Article 79 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Early childhood care and education for children below six years
Uniform civil code for the citizens
questions.x: Article 79: Constitution of Parliament.

questions.q: The right to privacy was declared a fundamental right by a nine-judge bench in:
o: Justice K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)
M. P. Sharma v. Satish Chandra (1954)
Kharak Singh v. State of U.P. (1962)
questions.x: Privacy was held intrinsic to Article 21 and the freedoms of Part III.

questions.q: 'Microfinance' in India is largely delivered through:
questions.x: Correct answer: Self-help groups and MFIs. The SHG–Bank Linkage Programme started in 1992.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the WTO:
1. Its highest decision-making body is the Ministerial Conference.
2. India is a founding member.
3. Its dispute settlement Appellate Body has been non-functional since December 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct; the Appellate Body has lacked quorum since 2019.

questions.q: In a simple banking model, the cash reserve ratio is 8% and banks keep no excess reserves. A fresh deposit of ₹800 crore can lead to a maximum total deposit creation of:
questions.x:
Deposit (money) multiplier = 1 / CRR = 1 / 0.08 = 12.5.
Total deposits = 800 × 12.5 = ₹10,000 crore (of which new credit = ₹9,200 crore).

questions.q: 'Repo rate' and 'bank rate' differ in that the bank rate:
o: Is a long-term rate charged without a repurchase agreement (used as penal rate benchmark)
Is set by the Finance Ministry
questions.x: Correct answer: Is a long-term rate charged without a repurchase agreement (used as penal rate benchmark). Bank rate is aligned with the MSF rate.

questions.q: The 'Lead Bank Scheme', under which a bank coordinates credit planning in a district, was introduced in:
questions.x: Correct answer: 1969. It followed the Gadgil Study Group's recommendation.

questions.q: The digital rupee (e₹), India's Central Bank Digital Currency, was piloted by the RBI from:
questions.x: The wholesale pilot began in November 2022 and retail in December 2022.

questions.q: The main thrust of the Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985–90) was:
o: Doubling per capita income in ten years; monitorable targets
Self-reliant and self-generating economy; disrupted by wars and drought, followed by plan holidays
questions.x: Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985–90): Food, work and productivity.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the RBI:
1. It acts as banker to the Government.
2. It is the lender of last resort for banks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct.
Both are core RBI functions.

questions.q: If MPC is 0.8, the investment multiplier is:
questions.x: Multiplier = 1/(1 − 0.8) = 5.

questions.q: The Y. V. Reddy (14th Finance Commission) is associated with:
o: Restructuring of the Food Corporation of India
Revising and strengthening the monetary policy framework
questions.x: Y. V. Reddy (14th Finance Commission): Devolution of central taxes for 2015–20.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹55,000; Purchases ₹2,90,000; Purchase returns ₹4,000; Carriage inwards ₹3,000; Sales ₹2,99,000; Sales returns ₹3,000; Closing stock ₹55,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 55,000 + 2,90,000 − 4,000 + 3,000 − 55,000 = ₹2,89,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 2,99,000 − 3,000 − 2,89,000 = ₹7,000.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: Preference shareholders have a preferential right over equity shareholders to:
o: Dividend and return of capital on winding up
questions.x: Correct answer: Dividend and return of capital on winding up. They get fixed dividends and priority in repayment.

questions.q: A machine is purchased for ₹4,45,000 and ₹7,000 is spent on its installation. Its estimated useful life is 8 years with a residual value of ₹8,000. Annual depreciation under the Straight Line Method is:
questions.x:
SLM depreciation = (Cost + installation − residual value) / useful life.
= (4,45,000 + 7,000 − 8,000) / 8 = 4,44,000 / 8 = ₹55,500 per year.
Installation is capitalised as part of cost (AS 10 / Ind AS 16).

questions.q: Ind AS 109 deals with:
questions.x: Ind AS 109 covers classification, measurement and impairment (expected credit loss) of financial instruments.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about errors:
1. Errors of principle affect the trial balance.
2. Posting an amount to the wrong side of an account affects the trial balance.
3. Omitting to post one side of an entry affects the trial balance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is incorrect; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Errors of principle do not affect the trial balance; one-sided errors do.

questions.q: 'Del credere commission' is paid to a consignee for:
o: Bearing the risk of bad debts on credit sales
questions.x: Correct answer: Bearing the risk of bad debts on credit sales. With del credere, bad debts are borne by the consignee.

questions.q: Legal expenses incurred to defend the title of land owned by the business are:
questions.x: Defending existing title maintains (does not enhance) the asset; legal costs of acquiring land would be capital.

questions.q: Provident fund deposits of government employees (GPF) are credited to:
questions.x: Moneys held in trust by the government, such as GPF and small savings, go to the Public Account.

questions.q: P and Q share profits in the ratio 2 : 3. They admit R for a 1/5 share, which R acquires from P and Q in their existing ratio. The new profit-sharing ratio of P, Q and R is:
Purchases during a month: 1st — 250 units @ ₹19; 10th — 200 units @ ₹22; 20th — 100 units @ ₹25. 450 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 100 units left come from the latest purchases: 100 × ₹25 = ₹2,500.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹4,500 at the middle of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 6% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 4,500 = ₹54,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the middle of each month = 6 months.
Interest = 54,000 × 6% × 6/12 = ₹1,620.

questions.q: The current ratio of a company is 1.75 : 1 and its working capital is ₹86,250. Its current assets amount to:
questions.x:
Let current liabilities = x. Then current assets = 1.75x and working capital = 1.75x − x = 0.75x.
0.75x = 86,250 → x = ₹1,15,000.
Current assets = 1.75 × 1,15,000 = ₹2,01,250.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹50,000 is depreciated at 20% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 3 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 50,000 × (0.8)^3 = ₹25,600.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹20,000.)

questions.q: Which of the following transactions will increase the current ratio when it is above 1 : 1?
questions.x: Issuing shares adds cash (a current asset) without adding current liabilities, so the ratio rises. Credit purchases raise both sides equally, which lowers a ratio above 1; buying machinery for cash and drawings reduce current assets.

questions.q: The 'Code of Discipline' in Indian industry, a voluntary tripartite code to prevent strikes and lock-outs without notice, was adopted in:
questions.x: Evolved at the 15th Indian Labour Conference (1957) and ratified by the central organisations of employers and workers in 1958.

questions.q: Under the bonus provisions, a newly set up establishment is generally liable to pay bonus from the accounting year in which:
o: It derives profit, or the sixth accounting year after sale of goods begins, whichever is earlier
questions.x: New establishments are exempt for the first five accounting years after commencing sale of goods/services, unless they make profit earlier.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, the retrenchment of a worker with at least one year of continuous service (in an establishment below the Chapter X threshold) requires:
o: One month's notice or wages in lieu, and retrenchment compensation
Six months' notice and approval of the High Court
questions.x: Conditions precedent: one month's written notice with reasons (or wages in lieu), retrenchment compensation, and notice to the government.

questions.q: Under Article 22 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948), everyone, as a member of society, has the right to:
questions.x: UDHR Article 22 recognises the right to social security; Article 23 covers right to work and just remuneration.

questions.q: Which form of industrial action involves workers staying inside the workplace but refusing to work?
questions.x: A sit-down or stay-in strike keeps workers on the premises; courts have viewed occupation of premises as unlawful trespass in some cases.

questions.q: Under the Code on Wages, a fine imposed on an employee for an act or omission cannot exceed what proportion of the wages payable for that wage period?
questions.x: Section 19 caps a fine at three per cent of wages payable in respect of the wage period, and it must be recovered within 90 days.

questions.q: An establishment has 120 workers; Union A has 70 members and Union B has 30 members. Under the IR Code, the negotiating arrangement will be:
o: A negotiating council of Unions A and B
Union B as the sole negotiating union
Union A as the sole negotiating union
questions.x: Union A has 70/120 ≈ 58%, above 51%, so it is the sole negotiating union.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, which authority recognises a trade union as a 'Central Trade Union' or 'State Trade Union'?
o: The Central or State Government, respectively
questions.x: The appropriate government may recognise a trade union or federation as a Central or State Trade Union for tripartite representation.

questions.q:
Consider the following thresholds under the Labour Codes:
1. Standing orders — 300 workers
2. Grievance Redressal Committee — 20 workers
3. Contract labour provisions — 50 contract workers
4. Factory with power — 10 workers
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
The first three are correct. The factory threshold with power is 20 workers (10 was the old Factories Act threshold).

questions.q: The Supreme Court established a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund with a contribution of ₹20,000 per child by offending employers in:
o: Unni Krishnan v. State of A.P. (1993)
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996)
questions.x: The case concerned child labour in the Sivakasi match and fireworks industry.

questions.q: 'Efficiency wage' theory explains why firms may pay above the market-clearing wage. The reason given is that higher wages:
o: Raise productivity by improving effort, morale and reducing turnover
questions.x: Higher wages can reduce shirking, attract better workers and lower turnover costs, making them profitable.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment added 'co-operative societies' to Article 19(1)(c) and inserted Article 43B?
questions.x: The 97th Amendment (2011) made forming co-operatives a fundamental right, added Article 43B and Part IXB.

questions.q: Under Part B of the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana, employers receive incentives of up to how much per month per additional employee?
questions.x: Employers get up to ₹3,000 per month per additional employee for two years (extended to the third and fourth years for manufacturing).

questions.q: Under the OSH Code, the occupier of a factory carrying on a hazardous process must constitute which committee with equal worker and management representation?
questions.x: Safety committees with equal representation of workers and management are required in factories carrying on hazardous processes and other notified establishments.

questions.q: The Supreme Court held that there is no automatic absorption of contract labour in the principal employer's establishment upon a notification abolishing contract labour in:
o: Gujarat Electricity Board v. Hind Mazdoor Sabha (1995)
Air India Statutory Corporation v. United Labour Union (1997)
Steel Authority of India Ltd v. National Union Waterfront Workers (2001)
questions.x: SAIL (2001), a Constitution Bench decision, overruled Air India (1997) on automatic absorption.

questions.q: The Employment Exchanges (Compulsory Notification of Vacancies) Act was enacted in:
questions.x: It required employers to notify vacancies to employment exchanges; it is now subsumed in the Code on Social Security.

questions.q: The 'Swavalamban' scheme (2010), which co-contributed to NPS accounts of unorganised sector workers, was replaced by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Atal Pension Yojana. Swavalamban subscribers were migrated to APY after 2015.

questions.q: The minimum pension under EPS 1995 is financed partly through:
o: Budgetary support from the Central Government
questions.x: The Government provides budgetary support to ensure the ₹1,000 minimum pension.

questions.q: NSAP is administered by the Ministry of:
questions.x: NSAP and its components are under the Ministry of Rural Development.

questions.q: Under the gratuity law, an employee's gratuity may be wholly or partially forfeited if the termination was for:
o: Riotous or disorderly conduct, or an offence involving moral turpitude in the course of employment
questions.x: Forfeiture is permitted for termination due to riotous/violent conduct or an offence involving moral turpitude.

questions.q: A member dies in service with average monthly wages of ₹15,000 over the last 12 months and an average PF balance entitling the maximum bonus. The EDLI benefit is:
questions.x: 35 × ₹15,000 = ₹5.25 lakh; adding the maximum bonus of ₹1.75 lakh gives ₹7 lakh, the cap.

questions.q: The eligible age group for PMSBY is:
questions.x: Correct answer: 18–70 years. Savings bank or post office account holders aged 18–70 can enrol.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): EPF is a defined contribution scheme while EPS 1995 is a defined benefit scheme.
Reason (R): Both EPF and EPS are funded only by employee contributions.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is correct. R is false — EPS is funded by the employer's 8.33% and the government's 1.16%; EPF gets both employer and employee shares.

questions.q: An employee draws basic wages plus DA of ₹20,000 per month and both employer and employee contribute 12% on actual wages. How much of the employer's share goes to the EPF (provident fund) account each month?
questions.x:
Employer's 12% of 20,000 = ₹2,400.
EPS share is capped at 8.33% of ₹15,000 = ₹1,250.
EPF share = 2,400 − 1,250 = ₹1,150.

questions.q: Section 17 of the EPF & MP Act deals with:
o: Exemption of establishments running their own PF trusts that are no less favourable
questions.x: Exempted establishments manage their own PF trusts under EPFO supervision, with benefits at least equal to the statutory scheme.

questions.q: At its October 2025 meeting the CBT decided to merge 13 partial-withdrawal provisions of the EPF Scheme into how many categories?
o: Five — one for each life event
Three — essential needs, housing needs and special circumstances
One single category with no conditions
questions.x: The 238th CBT meeting (13 October 2025) simplified partial withdrawals into three categories and allowed up to 100% of the eligible balance.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 12 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹440. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 12-week period including Sundays: 12 × 7 = 84 days.
Amount = ₹440 × 84 = ₹36,960. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹31,680.)

questions.q: Under UPS, in addition to the assured pension, a lump sum is paid at superannuation equal to:
o: One-tenth of monthly emoluments (pay + DA) for every completed six months of service
questions.x: Correct answer: One-tenth of monthly emoluments (pay + DA) for every completed six months of service. The lump sum does not reduce the assured pension.

questions.q: Which MS Excel function returns the number of cells that contain numbers?
questions.x: COUNTA counts non-empty cells.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Ice skating is possible because a thin layer of water forms under the blade.
Reason (R): Pressure and friction lower the melting point / generate heat to melt the surface ice.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Pressure melting and frictional heating create a lubricating layer.

questions.q: In computing, 'DNS' stands for:
questions.x: DNS = Domain Name System.

questions.q: The SI unit of absorbed radiation dose is the:
questions.x: Absorbed radiation dose is measured in Grays.

questions.q: Which organelle is the site of protein synthesis?
questions.x: Correct answer: Ribosome. Lysosomes are called 'suicide bags'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an operating system?
questions.x: Oracle is a database management system (and a company).

questions.q: In computing, 'ALU' stands for:
questions.x: ALU = Arithmetic Logic Unit.

questions.q: 'Track Changes' in MS Word is useful for:
o: Tracking the location of the file
Recording edits so reviewers can accept or reject them
questions.x: Correct answer: Recording edits so reviewers can accept or reject them. It supports collaborative editing.

questions.q: Sex of a child is determined by the:
o: Chromosome contributed by the father (X or Y)
questions.x: Correct answer: Chromosome contributed by the father (X or Y). Females are XX and males XY.

questions.q: A fire extinguisher using CO₂ puts out fire mainly by:
o: Cutting off the supply of oxygen
questions.x: Correct answer: Cutting off the supply of oxygen. Water should not be used on electrical or oil fires.

questions.q: Which plant hormone promotes fruit ripening?
questions.x: Correct answer: Ethylene. Auxins promote cell elongation; gibberellins promote stem growth.

questions.q: 'Digital arrest' scams typically involve:
o: Freezing of bank accounts by RBI
Blocking of social media accounts by courts
Fraudsters posing as police or officials on video calls and extorting money
questions.x: Correct answer: Fraudsters posing as police or officials on video calls and extorting money. No law enforcement agency arrests anyone over a video call.

questions.q: The monthly incomes of P and Q are in the ratio 8 : 5 and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 5 : 1. If each of them saves ₹14,875 a month, P's monthly income is:
questions.x:
Let incomes = 8k, 5k and expenditures = 5m, 1m.
8k − 5m = 5k − 1m = 14,875 → 3k = 4m.
Solving gives k = 3,500, m = 2,625.
P's income = 8 × 3,500 = ₹28,000 (check: ₹28,000 − ₹13,125 = ₹14,875).

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 7 : 6. After 12 years, the ratio will become 61 : 54. What is P's present age?
How many arrangements of the letters of 'DEPOSIT' are there in which the vowels are NOT all together?
questions.x:
Total arrangements = 5,040 (all letters are distinct).
Vowels together = 120 × 6 = 720.
Not all together = 5,040 − 720 = 4,320.

questions.q: A bag has 5 white and 8 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. What is the probability that at least one of them is white?
questions.x:
P(at least one white) = 1 − P(both black).
P(both black) = C(8,2)/C(13,2) = 28/78.
Required = 1 − 14/39 = 25/39.

questions.q: A field officer starts from point O and walks 18 km towards South, then turns right and walks 16 km, then turns right and walks 34 km, and finally turns right and walks 28 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: -18 +34 = 16 km → 16 km North.
East–West: -16 +28 = 12 km → 12 km East.
Distance = √(12² + 16²) = 20 km, towards North-East.

questions.q: a clerk and an assistant together can audit a ledger in 12 days. a clerk alone can do it in 21 days. How many days will an assistant alone take?
questions.x:
an assistant's one-day work = 1/12 − 1/21 = (21 − 12)/252 = 1/28.
So an assistant alone takes 28 days.

questions.q: The average of 13 observations is 41. The average of the first 7 is 45 and that of the last 7 is 46. The 7th observation is:
questions.x:
Sum of all 13 = 13 × 41 = 533.
First 7 + last 7 = 7×45 + 7×46 = 637; the middle observation is counted twice.
Middle = 637 − 533 = 104.

questions.q: ₹45,000 is invested for 1 year at 8% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly. The compound interest earned is:
questions.x:
Half-yearly: rate per period = 8/2 = 4%, number of periods = 2.
Amount = 45,000 × (1 + 4/100)² = ₹48,672.
CI = ₹3,672 (slightly more than annual compounding, which gives ₹3,600).

questions.q: In a row, Sonal is 19th from the left and Rekha is 15th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Sonal becomes 37th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Sonal occupies Rekha's old place, which is 15th from the right and now 37th from the left.
Total = 37 + 15 − 1 = 51.

questions.q: The number of claims settled by a regional office rises by 50%, then falls by 20%, and finally rises by 10%. The overall percentage change is:
questions.x:
Multiply the growth factors: (1 + 50/100) × (1 − 20/100) × (1 + 10/100) = 1.5 × 0.8 × 1.1 = 1.32.
Overall change = (1.32 − 1) × 100 = 32% → 32% increase.
Note: simply adding (50 − 20 + 10) is wrong because each change acts on a new base.

questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a reservoir in 9 hours and 18 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 10 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(9, 18, 10) = 90 units.
Rates: +10, +5, −9 units/hour → net 6 units/hour.
Time = 90 / 6 = 15 hours.

questions.q: In a certain code language, COURT is written as SQTNB. How is STRIKE written in that code?
questions.x:
Compare COURT → SQTNB: C→B, O→N, U→T…
Rule: the word is written in reverse order and then each letter is moved 1 place backward.
Applying it to STRIKE gives DJHQSR.

questions.q: Find the greatest number that will divide 715, 797, 1289 leaving the same remainder in each case.
questions.x:
If N leaves the same remainder, N divides the differences.
Differences: 797 − 715 = 82, 1289 − 797 = 492.
HCF(82, 492) = 82.

questions.q: Find the odd one out among 189, 35, 196 and 187.
questions.x: 189, 35, 196 are all multiples of 7; 187 is not. Hence 187 is the odd one out.
